messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

We can use the function to calculate number of solar panels needed. But they didn't provide average sunlight hours or usage efficiency. We could ask them for those values. Or we can assume defaults: average sunlight hours maybe 5 hours per day? usage_efficiency default 0.8. But the question: "How much electricity will I need" might refer to kWh per year. We can approximate using typical consumption per square foot. For US, average residential electricity consumption ~ 10-12 kWh per square foot per year? Actually typical consumption ~ 12 kWh per square foot per year? Wait typical US residential consumption ~ 10,000 kWh per year for 1,500 sq ft (~6.7 kWh/sqft). So for 2000 sq ft, maybe ~13,400 kWh/year. But we can also compute using the function: It calculates number of solar panels needed. That requires square_footage and average_sunlight_hours. We can ask for average sunlight hours. Let's ask clarifying question: "What is your average daily sunlight hours?" Also usage efficiency default 0.8. Then we can call function.
